name: Aurelythil
body:
The aurelythil are a rare species of winged humanoids who make their homes atop high mountains or in the sides of steep cliffs. Although they have avian features, they are believed to be descended from humans who long ago made a pact with winged, angelic beings, gaining their current form as result of magic rather than evolution.

Appearance

Aurelythil look similar to tall, noble humans—but with a few major differences.

The most significant of these are the two large feathered wings extending from their back. When fully outstretched, these wings span anywhere from 10 to 15 feet. When not flying, however, they are remarkably flexible, and an aurelythil can conceal them beneath a sturdy cloak with little difficulty.

In addition to their wings, aurelythil have birdlike talons for feet, and their heads are topped with ornate feathery displays rather than hair. In some individuals, the feathers that crest their heads are distinctly different from those on their wings.

Overall, aurelythil plumage coloration varies widely, and curiously their skin coloration usually matches this. Thus, white-feathered aurelythil have extremely pale, milky white skin, while blue-feathered aurelythil have skin the color of the sky. A few aurelythil even have brightly colored plumage like tropical birds, and their skin is likewise striped in reds, golds, and greens. In addition to the colors common to birds, some aurelythil have feathers of a more exotic nature, such as feathers with a golden or silver sheen.

Aurelythil eyes are large, but not unusually so, and come in an array of brilliant colors.

Social

Aurelythil lore differs as to the exact details of their origin story, but all agree that they are a people transformed by the grace of the gods. Some believe that they carry the blood of angels within their veins, while others say that it was powerful beings from the Elemental Planes of Air that blessed them with their wings. Whatever the truth, the aurelythil embraced their new life as a people transformed.

Today, they are known as a people who delight in every moment spent in flight.

Aurelythil are known as expert hunters, as well as lovers of sport and art. They are devoted to their families, and delight in meeting new people. While often seen as a thoughtful and serene people, they can be ruthless in defense of their homes and allies.

Aurelythil are protective of their land, but not overly aggressive toward travelers who are respectful. While they have trouble relating to ground-dwelling species, they respect those who are willing to engage with them peacefully, and are especially curious about those cultures that produce 4 items of significant artistic value. They especially delight in the company of elves, but also frequently barter with many other humanoids who pass through their lands.

While they value the craftsmanship of dwarves, they instinctively view anyone who dwells underground as suspicious.

Alignment and Religion

Most aurelythil are Chaotic Good, prizing their freedom and creativity, as well as the welfare of their community. They have a strong sense of justice, and most are also instilled with a strong sense of faith. The average aurelythil chooses a single patron deity to venerate—usually selecting one of the many empyreal lords, although some choose an elemental lord, an archfey, or a major deity whose interests include nature, weather, winds, or sky.

Common Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are perceptive and precise, but you tend to lean heavily on your own instincts rather than on any kind of education. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Wis, –2 Int [standard]. (0)
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size. (0)
Type You are a Humanoid with the aurelythil subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Aurelythil. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Auran, Celestial, Draconic, Elven, Giant, and Sylvan. (0)
Other Traits
Aurelythil Magic You add +1 to the DC of any saving throws against spells that you cast with the air descriptor. If your Charisma score is 12 or higher, you also gain the following spell-like abilities: 1/day—gust of wind, know direction, and message. The caster level for these effects is equal to your character level, and Charisma is your casting ability. (3)
Low-Light Vision You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Sky Hunter Fly, Perception, and Survival are always class skills for you. If you should also gain any of these skills as a class skill from levels you take in a class, then you gain a +1 species bonus with that skill. (2)
Wings You have two powerful, feathered wings that allow you to fly at a speed of 40 feet (poor maneuverability). You cannot fly while wearing heavy armor or carrying a heavy load. (6)
Total: 12 RP (advanced)
Variants
Aurelythil-blooded (Skylord)

Given their origin story, it is not surprising that some aurelythil—although rare— actually display concrete evidence of divine blood. While their appearance isn’t that different from normal aurelythil, they are outsiders with the native subtype and are considered aasimars for the purposes of species.

As a skylord, you gain the following alternate aasimar traits:

Alternate Ability Scores You gain +2 Dex and +2 Wis.
Aurelythil Traits You gain the aurelythil magic and wings species traits, as an aurelythil. These traits replace celestial resistances, skilled, and spell-like ability.
Alternate Traits

Each of the following options replace one or more common other traits.

Blessings of the Wind If your Wisdom score is 12 or higher, you gain the following spell-like abilities: 1/day—breeze*, guidance, and with the wind. The caster level for these effects is equal to your character level. This trait replaces aurelythil magic.
Flyby You gain Flyby Attack B1 as a bonus feat at 1st level. This trait replaces aurelythil magic.
Night Hunter You receive a +2 species bonus to Perception and Stealth checks made in dim light or darkness. This trait replaces sky hunter.
Sky Weapons You are proficient with the bolas, shortbow, short spear, and spear. You gain a +1 bonus on attack rolls with any of these weapons when you use them while flying. This trait replaces sky hunter.
Talons While flying, you can use your feet to make two talon attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d4 slashing damage each. This trait replaces sky hunter.
Vanguard Your bold personality outshines all of those around you, making you a natural leader among your people— although at times this trait can get in the way of your better judgment. You gain a +2 bonus to Charisma instead of a +2 bonus to Wisdom. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1 foot to your fly speed while raging. This option has no effect unless you have selected it five times (or another increment of five).
Bard Add +1 to your number of bardic performance rounds per day.
Bloodrager Add +1 foot to your fly speed while bloodraging. This option has no effect unless you have selected it five times (or another increment of five).
Cleric Add a +1 bonus on caster level checks made to overcome the spell resistance of outsiders.
Druid Add +1/4 to your caster level when casting druid spells with the air descriptor.
Fighter Add +1/2 to your CMD while flying.
Hunter Increase the fly speed of your animal companion by 1 foot. In combat, this has no effect unless you select this option 5 times (or another increment of 5). If you ever replace your animal companion, the new animal companion gains this bonus to its fly speed. This benefit cannot grant a fly speed to your companion, only increase a fly speed your companion already has.
Inquisitor Add a +1/2 bonus on Survival checks and a +1/2 bonus Knowledge checks to identify creatures.
Monk Add a +1/3 bonus on critical hit confirmation rolls for attacks made with unarmed strikes or natural weapons 7 (maximum bonus of +5). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Paladin You gain energy resistance 1 against cold, electricity, or sonic. Each time you selects this reward, increase your resistance to one of these energy types by 1 (maximum 10 for any one type).
Ranger Add a +1/2 bonus on wild empathy checks to influence animals and magical beasts with a natural fly speed.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Perception and Stealth checks made while flying.
Shaman Add +5 feet to the range of a chosen shaman hex. Multiple bonuses from this ability can apply to the same hex, to a maximum of an additional 30 feet for any single hex.
Slayer Choose a weapon from the following list: talons, bolas, shortbow, short spear, or spear. Add a +1/2 bonus to sneak attack damage with the weapon chosen.
Sorcerer Add +1/4 to your caster level when casting sorcerer spells with the air descriptor.
Warpriest Add a +1/2 bonus to Knowledge (nature) and Knowledge (planes) checks.
Witch Your familiar gains resistance 1 against cold, electricity, or sonic. Each time you select this reward, increase the familiar’s resistance to one of these energy types by 1 (maximum 5 for any one type). If you ever replaces your familiar, the new familiar has these resistances.
